title: Soft-Body Portrait Studio
description: An antique camera sits on a tripod facing a soft-body face sculpture made of jelly-like material. The user pokes and stretches the face to create funny expressions, then clicks the camera's shutter button to 'capture' the deformed portrait, which freezes as a polaroid thumbnail on screen.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a soft-body portrait studio scene. Load both GLB assets using GLTFLoader: place AntiqueCamera.glb on the left side of the scene on a small pedestal, and facecap.glb centered and facing the camera model. Implement a spring-mass soft-body simulation on the face mesh: on load, extract the face geometry vertices and build a network of spring constraints connecting neighboring vertices (use rest lengths from original positions, spring stiffness 0.3, damping 0.95). Each frame, integrate forces (light gravity downward, spring restoration) and update the geometry vertex positions with needsUpdate flags. Interaction steps: (1) User hovers over the face and sees a highlight glow indicating it is interactive. (2) User clicks and drags on the face mesh using raycasting to pull vertices outward, deforming the jelly face with a radial falloff influence radius of 0.15 units. (3) On release, the face wobbles back via spring forces with visible oscillation. (4) User can repeat pokes to create exaggerated expressions by dragging nose, cheeks, or forehead. (5) User clicks directly on the antique camera model (raycast hit detection) to trigger a shutter action: play a CSS flash animation (white overlay fading out), freeze the current deformed face state, and render a small 128x128 thumbnail using a secondary orthographic camera aimed at the face, displayed as a polaroid-style card in the bottom-right corner of the screen with a CSS border and drop shadow. Allow up to 4 polaroid captures that stack with slight rotation offsets. Set up the main PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 1.2, 3) looking at origin. Add warm studio lighting: a soft warm SpotLight (0xffe4b5) from above-left, a dim fill HemisphereLight, and a subtle RectAreaLight behind the camera model simulating a studio lamp. Use OrbitControls with limited vertical rotation so the user can orbit slightly but stays focused on the scene. Background should be a dark warm gradient using scene.background with a Color of 0x2a1a0e.
